transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-04
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Daniel Park (Aeon Head of ML), Sara Lind (Aeon Platform Eng), Rashid Khan (Aeon CTO - joined late), Liam (Product)

Summary:
Quick scout/discovery to validate model choice, context length needs, multilingual support, and whether hosted/dedicated/private is the right path for Aeon. Customer is sensitive to latency and data residency; they want a pilot to benchmark open models and tool-calling with their retrieval system.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and infra constraints
- Throughput & latency SLOs, cost tradeoffs
- Context length and multi-lingual requirements
- Tool-calling (retrieval, connectors, external APIs)
- Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SSO
- Next steps and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, shall we do quick intros? I'm Maya, AE at Redwood Inference.
[00:06] Daniel Park: Hey Maya, Daniel here. Head of ML at Aeon. We run a mixture of microservices and a data lake, mostly in GCP for now.
[00:11] Sara Lind: Sara, platform eng. I manage our infra and network.
[00:14] Omar Rodriguez: Omar, solutions engineer at Redwood, I'll jump into performance questions.
[00:18] Liam: Liam, PM — here to represent product requirements.
[00:20] Rashid Khan: Rashid — CTO, I might drop on and off, got another meeting.
[00:24] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda: understand the workload, what success looks like, constraint, and then model and deploy options — hosted, dedicated, or private. Sound ok?
[00:31] Daniel Park: Perfect. To give context: we have a customer-support assistant and a knowledge hub that needs retrieval-augmented generation. Peak is about 150 qps, but 95th is closer to 50 sustained. Latency target is 200-300ms p50 for short answers, up to 800ms is acceptable for long-form.
[00:47] Omar Rodriguez: Okay, are those end-to-end or token-only?
[00:50] Daniel Park: End-to-end from request to transient response, inc network. Our current prod is a mix — some calls hit external LLMs. Cost is a big factor, we want predictability.
[00:59] Sara Lind: Also want to keep data in our project and maintain audit trails. SOC2 is in flight, and we have some regulated customers in EU so data residency matters.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Yep, that maps well to our common patterns. Quick question on context length — how much context do you expect to send?
[01:18] Liam: For support we usually send last 8 messages plus a doc chunk, so roughly 6-8k tokens typical, some escalations up to 40k token-ish when we include long logs.
[01:30] Omar Rodriguez: 40k — okay that pushes towards long context models or retrieval + chunking. Are you expecting multilingual?
[01:36] Daniel Park: Yes. About 15% of traffic is Spanish, Portuguese, and a little French and Japanese. We also want to do normalization across languages.
[01:44] Maya Chen: Great. So the initial scope is: open model comparison, throughput sizing, multilingual quality, tool-calling with your retrieval layer, and then decide between hosted/dedicated/private based on cost and residency.
[01:53] Rashid Khan: I joined — sorry — quick note on KMS, we use Cloud KMS and want HSM-backed keys for private deployments.
[01:59] Omar Rodriguez: Noted. We support KMS integrations for private and dedicated. Hosted has customer-managed encryption options with bring-your-own-keys on some tiers.
[02:08] Sara Lind: How does Redwood handle KV cache and prefix caching? We saw some demos where prefix caching helped reduce cost but were worried about cache invalidation.
[02:17] Omar Rodriguez: The runtime does automatic KV prefix caching where useful; you can configure TTLs and invalidation hooks. There is also a shared warm-up cache for continuous batching, but for private deploy we give you full control.
[02:29] Daniel Park: Good. On model selection, we were evaluating Llama variants, Mistral, and some of the LongContext models — Mistral XL? Also heard about the new long-form open weights that claim 100k contexts; curious about tradeoffs.
[02:41] Maya Chen: Two axes: token throughput & cost vs context length & quality. Long-context models often incur more memory and slower per-token throughput, and some are still experimental on quantization. For many workflows, a mid-size long-context model plus an effective retrieval pipeline hits the sweet spot.
[02:55] Liam: For tool-calling, we need deterministic function calls — e.g., call our search API, call a DB write, and then format final answer. Does Redwood support function/tool calls?
[03:05] Omar Rodriguez: Yes, we have function calling and structured output support. For hosted we expose hooks and we can stream function-call events. For Private/Dedicated we can integrate directly with your internal connectors and webhook systems.
[03:18] Sara Lind: Security question: audit logs — do we get per-request logs and token-level cost attribution? Our compliance team needs tracing tied to user IDs.
[03:27] Maya Chen: Yes, our Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route tracing, and you can wire audit logs to your logging backend. For private deployments those logs can stay in your VPC.
[03:37] Daniel Park: About latency — if we want 200-300ms p50 for short answers, is hosted realistic, or do we need dedicated capacity?
[03:45] Omar Rodriguez: Hosted can hit low latency for small models and short contexts; however, for guaranteed p50 under load and consistent p95 SLOs dedicated is safer. Dedicated with pinned GPU pools gives more predictable throughput. Private will be similar to dedicated but with more network variability unless co-located.
[04:00] Liam: Cost sensitivity — can you give a rough delta hosted vs dedicated?
[04:03] Maya Chen: Very rough: hosted is pay-as-you-go — higher per-token but no infra commitment. Dedicated is lower per-token at committed throughput — say 20-40% cheaper at scale depending on model and utilization. Private has higher fixed ops cost but gives control for compliance. We'll send detailed pricing scenarios.
[04:18] Daniel Park: For benchmarks — we want to test Spanish performance, long-context (~20-40k), and tool-calling correctness. Can Redwood run those tests?
[04:26] Omar Rodriguez: Yes. Proposed pilot: Redwood runs a 2-week pilot on dedicated capacity with a curated set of 5 prompts per use-case and your retrieval layer attached. We'll run throughput/load tests and a correctness pass. Alternatively we can give you the harness to run in your private env.
[04:40] Sara Lind: We prefer to run the harness in our VPC for compliance, but we may start with Redwood-hosted benchmarks for speed.
[04:47] Maya Chen: Makes sense. We'll include both options in the follow-up.
[04:50] Rashid Khan: One more — what about multi-version rollouts? We need canary deploys and quick fallback if a model regression happens.
[04:57] Omar Rodriguez: Redwood Console supports rollouts, canary, A/B, and automatic fallbacks to a lower-cost or more robust variant. You can pin per-route model versions. There are also regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[05:08] Daniel Park: Okay, real-world constraints — our data egress limits and VPC peering are critical. If we do private, can Redwood work with our network team to set up peering and dedicated links?
[05:18] Maya Chen: Yes, for Private we have a VPC onboarding checklist and engineering runbook. We'll coordinate with your network team.
[05:24] Liam: On multilingual quality, do you recommend one model for all languages or separate region-specific models?
[05:29] Omar Rodriguez: Often one multilingual model suffices for lighter traffic, but for high-quality region-specific nuance you may want language-specialized models for critical flows. That's part of what we'll test.
[05:38] Daniel Park: Can Redwood host quantized variants for dedicated to cut cost? We've seen memory-constrained quantized 4-bit variants that dramatically reduce cost but sometimes impact quality.
[05:47] Omar Rodriguez: Yes — Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload. We test LLM quantization tradeoffs and can run a quality/regression alert if you enable a quantized variant.
[05:57] Sara Lind: Are there constraints for on-prem hardware? Our hardware ops team prefers NVIDIA H100 clusters but some satellite offices have A100s.
[06:06] Maya Chen: The runtime supports both, and we do kernel selection at compile-time for each instance. For private we document recommended instance types and bin packing profiles.
[06:14] Daniel Park: Great. Any red flags or things we should watch for?
[06:18] Omar Rodriguez: Watch for tokenization mismatches and prompt engineering across languages — that can cause unpredictable token counts and cost. Also KV cache invalidation across frequently updated docs can be tricky.
[06:28] Liam: On timeline — we want a decision in 6 weeks to start pilot in Q3. Is that feasible?
[06:34] Maya Chen: Totally feasible. We'll put together a pilot plan and pricing by Friday.
[06:38] Rashid Khan: I'm out — thanks all.
[06:40] Maya Chen: Thanks Rashid.
[06:42] Omar Rodriguez: Quick demo note — we'll attach sample latency/throughput graphs in our follow-up.
[06:46] Daniel Park: Also please include notes on how function calls are audited — we need to show that to compliance.
[06:52] Maya Chen: Will do.
[06:54] Sara Lind: One small thing — our security team will want the SAML SSO flow and RBAC mapping for audit.
[06:59] Priya Nair: We'll include SSO, RBAC mapping doc and a private deployment checklist.
[07:05] Maya Chen: Okay, let's recap action items.
[07:08] Daniel Park: Sounds good.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Redwood to send hosted vs dedicated pricing, committed throughput examples, and cost calc by 2027-05-07.
- Omar to prepare benchmark harness and sample scripts; offer both hosted run and VPC-run options.
- Daniel to share 5 representative prompts and a couple production traces for accuracy/latency testing by 2027-05-06.
- Sara to confirm compliance reviewers and KMS provider details by 2027-05-08.
